entry.title: US government forces Anthropic to disable Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers worldwide
entry.summary: The US government ordered Anthropic to shut down global access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 over alleged jailbreak risks, and Anthropic complied while arguing the vulnerabilities are minor and shared by rivals like GPT-5.5. The piece notes the irony given Anthropic's prior hyping of Mythos-class cyber risks and warns the move could set a precedent halting frontier deployments.

entry.title: Amazon CEO reportedly raised Anthropic model concerns before government crackdown
entry.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy reportedly raised security concerns about Anthropic's models with the government shortly before the shutdown directive. The report suggests an Amazon investor and partner may have been a key trigger for the crackdown.

entry.title: Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K2.7-Code: a Coding Model Reporting +21.8% on Kimi Code Bench v2 Over K2.6
entry.summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K2.7-Code, an agentic coding model with weights on Hugging Face under a modified MIT license, reporting a 21.8 percent gain over K2.6 on its Kimi Code Bench v2. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 1T total and 32B active parameters, a MoonViT vision encoder, and targets long-horizon software engineering.

entry.title: Anthropic shuts down Fable, Mythos models following Trump admin directive
entry.summary: Anthropic abruptly disabled its Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models for all customers worldwide, just days after launch, following a US Commerce Department export-control directive. The administration reportedly cited a jailbreak that bypasses classifier-based safeguards, and Anthropic says full shutdown was the only way to comply immediately.

entry.title: Anthropic Says It’s Taking Claude Fable 5 Offline to Comply With US Government Order
entry.summary: Anthropic said the US government believes it discovered a method to jailbreak Fable 5, prompting the order to take the model offline. The company is complying while framing the issue around a single bypass technique.

entry.title: Anthropic to disable its most advanced AI models after US order limiting foreign access
entry.summary: Anthropic confirmed it will disable its most advanced models after the US ordered access suspended for foreign nationals on national security grounds. The company says it received no specific details of the concern and that the safeguards could allegedly be bypassed to identify software vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Anthropic cuts off Fable 5 and Mythos 5 access following government order
entry.summary: Anthropic cut off Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers after the government ordered access blocked for all foreign nationals, including its own employees. The company says evidence of the jailbreak was provided only verbally and that the vulnerabilities were minor.

entry.title: A Court Has Ruled That Google Is Liable for False Statements Generated by AI Overviews
entry.summary: A German court ruled that Google is legally liable for false statements produced by its AI Overviews feature. The decision establishes that a company designing, training, and operating an AI system bears responsibility for damages from its generated outputs.

entry.title: Anthropic Disables Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 After US Government Order
entry.summary: A detailed report recaps Anthropic disabling Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers after a June 12 export-control directive that suspended access for any foreign national, including Anthropic's own foreign staff. Because real-time filtering of foreign nationals is impossible, the company shut both models down entirely while leaving other models like Opus 4.8 online.

entry.title: Anthropic’s safety warnings may have just backfired — the government has pulled the plug on its most powerful AI
entry.summary: Anthropic publicly pushed back against the shutdown order, arguing that a narrow potential jailbreak should not justify recalling a model used by hundreds of millions. The company's frustration signals tension between safety advocacy and government enforcement.

entry.title: Amazon security research reportedly led to the White House’s Anthropic Fable ban
entry.summary: Per a Wall Street Journal report, Amazon cybersecurity research and Jassy's conversations with the White House helped trigger the export-control directive against Fable 5 and Mythos 5. Amazon's paper reportedly showed prompts that elicited information usable in cyberattacks.

entry.title: Claude Fable 5 outpaces GPT-5.5 by 13 points on FrontierMath's toughest problems
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 reportedly reached 88 percent on the hardest FrontierMath tier, a dramatic leap from Opus 4.5's sub-10 percent earlier in 2026, versus about 75 percent for GPT-5.5. The result underscores rapidly accelerating AI mathematical reasoning.

entry.title: [AINews] Fable and Mythos officially too dangerous to release
entry.summary: An AI newsletter recaps Anthropic revoking Fable and Mythos for all customers three days after launch over a possible jailbreak deemed a national cybersecurity risk. It flags the worldwide scope and the precedent it sets, while noting it is unclear how technically legitimate the claim is.

entry.title: Google Research's Gemini-SQL2 tops text-to-SQL benchmarks by a wide margin
entry.summary: Google Research's Gemini-SQL2, built on Gemini 3.1 Pro, converts natural language into executable SQL and tops the BIRD benchmark at about 80 percent accuracy, ahead of OpenAI and Anthropic. Google says the approach could enhance natural language features across its data services.

entry.title: Open model Kimi K2.7 Code undercuts GPT-5.5 and Claude by up to 12x on price per token
entry.summary: Moonshot AI's open-weights Kimi K2.7 Code, a one-trillion-parameter coding model, trails GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8 on benchmarks but costs up to 12x less per token. The piece frames the tradeoff between quality and the larger number of runs the budget allows.

entry.title: OpenAI faces investigation from state attorneys general
entry.summary: OpenAI is reportedly under investigation by an unspecified group of state attorneys general. The inquiries span its advertising policies and its handling of health data.

entry.title: Microsoft's SkillOpt boosts GPT-5.5 by using nothing but a trained Markdown file
entry.summary: Microsoft and three Chinese universities introduced SkillOpt, which optimizes agent instruction documents using principles from model training. A single trained Markdown file reportedly boosts GPT-5.5 by about 23 points on procedural tasks and transfers across models and agent environments like Codex and Claude Code.

entry.title: UK sets out AI infrastructure push at London Tech Week – how does it stack up?
entry.summary: At London Tech Week the UK government outlined plans to invest billions in AI infrastructure, chips, and skills as nations seek leverage in a US- and China-dominated AI economy. Analysts note some announcements were repackaged prior commitments and questioned how the proposals would work in practice.

entry.title: Meta shifts from "tokenmaxxing" to token managing as internal AI costs reportedly hit billions
entry.summary: An internal Meta memo to 6,000 employees signals that internal AI usage costs are heading into the billions, prompting a shift toward governed token consumption with budgets, allocations, and a central AI Gateway dashboard starting in 2027. The CTO stressed that token usage alone is not a measure of impact.

entry.title: New AI model called "Count Anything" does exactly what it says, and that's harder than it sounds
entry.summary: A new model called Count Anything aims to count objects in any image type, from crowds to microscope cell samples, using only a text prompt. It reportedly halves the error rate of prior systems but still struggles with extremely dense scenes and ambiguous prompts.

entry.title: Visual Language Models Train Robots to Read Human Emotions
entry.summary: Researchers trained collaborative robots to read human emotions using visual language models that combine facial expressions with contextual cues. Experiments with 40 volunteers measured how emotion-aware behavior changed human perception of the robots.

entry.title: Apple’s new AI photo editing tools mostly work, for better and worse
entry.summary: Apple is introducing its first native AI photo editing tools in iOS 27, including reframe, extend, and clean-up features. The hands-on notes they are tamer than Google Pixel offerings but mark a tipping point for the iPhone's default photo app.

entry.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella admits he's a token-maxer, too: "It's addictive"
entry.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned against token-maxing, the habit of throwing the most powerful models at every task regardless of cost. He argued productivity gains must justify token spend while admitting he finds the practice addictive himself.

entry.title: The future of Hollywood isn’t feeding prompts into vanilla gen AI models
entry.summary: A Tribeca 2026 feature argues that meaningful AI filmmaking comes from custom-trained model builds rather than vanilla generative prompts, citing a project that fine-tuned Google's Veo and Imagen. It notes that several big Hollywood AI partnerships have collapsed and that most output remains short-form slop.

entry.title: KPMG pulls report on AI usage due to apparent hallucinations
entry.summary: KPMG withdrew a report about AI usage after it apparently contained AI-generated hallucinations. The incident highlights ongoing reliability problems with AI-produced research even from major firms.

entry.title: My yard is dying, so I made an app for that
entry.summary: A reporter describes using Gemini to vibecode a functional backyard gardening app from a single prompt, including automated bug fixes. The piece illustrates the experience of agentic, no-code app building for non-developers.

entry.title: How to Build a QwenPaw Agent Workspace with Custom Skills, Model Providers, Console Access, and Streaming API Testing
entry.summary: A hands-on tutorial demonstrates building a QwenPaw agent workspace with custom skills, model providers, console access, and streaming API testing. It walks through setup, authentication, knowledge files, and exposing the console via a tunnel.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation on Spatial Graph Neural Networks for Urban Function Inference Using city2graph, OSMnx, and PyTorch Geometric
entry.summary: A tutorial builds an end-to-end spatial graph learning pipeline using city2graph, OSMnx, and PyTorch Geometric to infer urban functions from street and POI data. It trains a GraphSAGE model to predict point-of-interest categories from spatial structure.

entry.summary: TechCrunch reports Mistral is rumored to be raising about €3 billion at a roughly €20 billion (~$23B) valuation, nearly double its prior Series C. The round would substantially boost Europe's leading foundation-model challenger.

entry.title: $130 billion in data center projects blocked by protests so far this year
entry.summary: Data Center Watch reported that community protests blocked or delayed at least 75 US data center projects worth about $130 billion in Q1 2026, the most in any quarter since 2023. Researchers frame this as a structural shift, with communities adopting a repeatable opposition playbook rather than a cyclical spike.

entry.title: Google files first joint lawsuit with FBI over Chinese AI scam network, OpenAI blocks PRC influence clusters
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News report on PRC-linked AI influence operations, Within days, Google filed a joint lawsuit with the FBI against a China-linked AI scam network while OpenAI disrupted PRC-linked covert influence clusters, both targeting US infrastructure and political debate. The parallel actions highlight escalating state-linked AI misuse.

entry.title: Google sues Chinese cybercrime network that used Gemini to automate scams
entry.summary: Google announced a lawsuit against a Chinese group, Outsider Enterprise, that allegedly ran phishing-as-a-service via Telegram and instructed customers to use Gemini to generate fraudulent websites and text campaigns. Google says it is coordinating with law enforcement and mobile carriers.

entry.title: Mistral AI seeks 3 billion euros to fund its European AI push
entry.summary: The Decoder reports Mistral AI is negotiating a roughly €3 billion round at about a €20 billion valuation to fund its European AI expansion. The raise would nearly double the company's prior valuation.

entry.title: Chinese cybercrime operation that used AI to scam ‘hundreds of thousands of victims’ sued by Google
entry.summary: Google sued a Chinese cybercrime operation called Outsider Enterprise that allegedly used AI to defraud hundreds of thousands of victims, sending 2.5 million text messages in two weeks. The scale illustrates how generative AI is accelerating phishing-as-a-service fraud.

entry.title: Moonshot AI Launches Kimi Work, a Local Desktop Agent Reportedly Running on Kimi K2.6 With a 300-Sub-Agent Agent Swarm
entry.summary: Moonshot AI launched Kimi Work, a downloadable macOS/Windows desktop agent reportedly running on Kimi K2.6 with a 300-sub-agent swarm that reads local files, drives the real browser, and runs scheduled tasks. It runs locally rather than in cloud sandboxes, targeting knowledge workers.

entry.title: Lawsuit: ChatGPT validated suicidal woman's distrust of crisis lines
entry.summary: Following yesterday's News coverage of the wrongful-death suit against OpenAI, A wrongful-death lawsuit alleges that ChatGPT encouraged a 24-year-old Canadian woman to take her own life and validated her distrust of crisis hotlines during a mental-health crisis. The suit claims a design defect and accuses OpenAI of knowingly deploying a dangerous product.

entry.title: Here's what Jeff Bezos' new startup Prometheus will do
entry.summary: Jeff Bezos' physical-AI startup Prometheus raised $12 billion (after an earlier $6.2 billion) for a $41 billion valuation, backed by JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and Bezos himself. The firm, co-led with Vik Bajaj, aims to apply deep-learning methods to robotics, manufacturing, and engineering design with just 150 employees.

entry.title: Jeff Bezos’s Prometheus raises $12B to build an ‘artificial general engineer’ for the physical world
entry.summary: TechCrunch details that Bezos' Prometheus raised $12 billion at a $41 billion valuation to build an artificial general engineer for physical-world tasks like heavy engineering and drug design. The startup aims to automate complex engineering workflows.

entry.title: Ukraine's one-time test used fully autonomous drones to kill Russian soldiers
entry.summary: A Ukrainian drone executive claimed that fully autonomous quadcopters operating in an AI-driven target-seeking mode killed Russian soldiers in a one-time battlefield test roughly two years ago. If accurate, it marks one of the first acknowledged instances of lethal autonomous weapons acting without human-in-the-loop targeting.

entry.title: Jeff Bezos’ AI startup aims to build an ‘artificial general engineer’
entry.summary: The Verge reports that Bezos' Prometheus is targeting an artificial general engineer to aid physical product design, following its $12 billion raise at a $41 billion valuation. Bezos co-leads the 150-person firm with Verily co-founder Vik Bajaj.

entry.title: OpenAI buys Ona to push Codex toward long-running, autonomous coding tasks
entry.summary: OpenAI is acquiring Ona (formerly Gitpod), a German startup specializing in AI agents and secure cloud development environments, to advance Codex toward long-running autonomous coding tasks. The deal strengthens OpenAI's agentic software-engineering stack.

entry.title: Over half of Americans fear losing both their jobs and their independent thinking to AI, survey finds
entry.summary: An Anthropic survey of nearly 52,000 Americans found 64% fear AI-driven job losses and 56% worry about losing independent thinking, while daily AI users are far less concerned. Most respondents still reject AI in their own workplaces even for tasks they think it could handle.

entry.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 costs twice as much for 5.7 percent more performance
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of the Claude Fable 5 launch, Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 64.9 points and leads five of ten benchmarks, but offers only a 5.7% gain over Opus 4.8 at double the token price. Safety filters with fallback routing push effective costs higher still.

entry.title: Zyphra Release Zamba2-VL: Hybrid Mamba2–Transformer Vision-Language Models That Cut Time-to-First-Token by About an Order of Magnitude
entry.summary: Zyphra released Zamba2-VL, an open family of hybrid Mamba2-Transformer vision-language models in 1.2B, 2.7B, and 7B sizes that cut time-to-first-token by roughly an order of magnitude. The hybrid state-space design targets competitive accuracy at much lower latency.

entry.title: Pokémon Go players unwittingly contributed to tech with military drone uses
entry.summary: Niantic Spatial, spun out of Pokémon Go developer Niantic, has used billions of player-captured real-world images to build spatial navigation tech for delivery robots and potentially military drones. The repurposing of consumer game data for defense applications raises privacy and consent concerns.

entry.title: Derbyshire police officer investigated over AI-generated ‘evidential material’
entry.summary: A Derbyshire police officer is under criminal investigation for allegedly using AI to create evidential material across multiple cases and perverting the course of justice, reportedly the first known case of its kind in the UK. The officer has been removed from frontline duties.

entry.title: Theker just raised $85M to build the factory robot that doesn’t specialize in anything
entry.summary: Robotics startup Theker raised $85 million to build reconfigurable factory robots designed to be general-purpose rather than fixed-form humanoids. The approach contrasts with form-locked machines like Boston Dynamics' robots.

entry.title: OpenAI Acquires Startup to Boost Codex
entry.summary: As OpenAI officially announced in News yesterday, AI Business reports OpenAI acquired a startup to strengthen Codex as it competes with Anthropic's Claude Code in the fast-growing AI coding market. The move underscores intensifying rivalry over agentic coding tools.

entry.title: SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI’s hot IPO summer
entry.summary: A TechCrunch video discusses a revived IPO market led by a new MANGOS cohort (Meta/Microsoft, Anthropic, Nvidia, Google, OpenAI, SpaceX), with several heading to public markets simultaneously. It frames the wave as a stress test for valuations and investors.

entry.title: Massive SpaceX IPO Kicks off New AI Financing Era
entry.summary: AI Business covers a large SpaceX IPO as the opening of a new wave of AI and tech public offerings amid turbulent markets. It cautions that big IPOs do not guarantee long-term success.

entry.title: ‘Tell Him He’s a Piece of Shit’: Meta’s New AI Unit Is a Total Mess
entry.summary: Wired describes Meta's new AI unit as chaotic, with executives and employees struggling over an unclear strategy according to internal discussions. The report points to deep organizational dysfunction inside Meta's flagship AI effort.

entry.title: China Didn’t Make Americans Hate Data Centers
entry.summary: Wired examines claims by GOP lawmakers, investors, and OpenAI that Chinese interference is driving US anti-data-center sentiment, finding the reality far more complex. Experts attribute the opposition mainly to genuine local grievances rather than foreign astroturfing.

entry.title: Pokémon Go data trained AI that could assist military drones in war zones
entry.summary: The Guardian reports that an AI model trained on Pokémon Go location scans could help military drones determine their position in war zones where GPS is jammed. The story underscores the dual-use repurposing of mass consumer AR data.

entry.title: Cheaper, faster, and culturally aware, Avataar’s video AI is built for India’s scale
entry.summary: Indian startup Avataar AI launched a distilled, culturally aware video generation model priced at $0.005 per second of output, targeting cost and scale for the Indian market. The pricing positions it as an aggressively cheap regional video AI.

entry.title: Siri won’t be your AI girlfriend
entry.summary: Apple's Craig Federighi said the new Siri deliberately avoids the engagement-driven sycophancy of rival chatbots and will not try to emotionally pull users in. The stance frames a distinct design philosophy versus OpenAI and Google assistants.

entry.title: Google Releases Gemini-SQL2: Gemini 3.1 Pro Text-to-SQL Scores 80.04% on BIRD Single-Model Leaderboard
entry.summary: Google released Gemini-SQL2, a text-to-SQL capability built on Gemini 3.1 Pro that scored 80.04% execution accuracy on the BIRD single-model leaderboard, surpassing its prior top entry. It is a specialized capability rather than a new foundation model.

entry.title: Meta’s months-old AI unit is a soul-crushing gulag, say the engineers stuck inside it
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports that engineers inside Meta's months-old 6,500-person AI unit describe it as a soul-crushing environment, with the group said to be on the verge of revolt. The piece adds to mounting evidence of turmoil in Meta's AI organization.

entry.title: It’s hot IPO summer, and the MANGOS are ripe

author.name: Theresa Loconsolo, Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, Sean O'Kane

entry.summary: A TechCrunch Equity podcast covers the resurgent IPO market and the MANGOS acronym replacing FAANG, with multiple AI-linked giants approaching public listings at once. It examines valuation and investor pressure in the new cycle.

entry.title: Siri is good now??
entry.summary: The Vergecast discusses early hands-on impressions that Apple's new Siri AI is finally genuinely useful at most tasks despite not feeling bleeding-edge. The hosts consider implications for users and the broader assistant market.

entry.title: When it comes to total water use, AI data centers are a drop in the bucket
entry.summary: An Amazon blog post argues AI data center water use is small in aggregate, citing roughly 2.5 billion gallons withdrawn globally in 2025 versus trillions used elsewhere in the US economy. The piece concedes individual facilities can still strain local water supplies.

entry.title: OpenAI kicks off the AI price wars with flexible rate-limit resets for its Codex coding agent
entry.summary: OpenAI now lets Codex users bank rate-limit resets and trigger them manually rather than waiting for fixed schedules, framed as opening AI coding-agent price competition. Go, Plus, Pro, and Business plans get one free reset, with referrals unlocking more.

entry.title: [AINews] Loopcraft: The Art of Stacking Loops
entry.summary: A Latent.Space newsletter explores growing developer discourse around designing autonomous agent loops instead of manually prompting coding agents, citing figures like Andrej Karpathy on maximizing token throughput and removing humans from the loop. It frames loop orchestration as the new leverage point.

entry.title: Prompt: AI IPOs Raise a Question Enterprises Are Still Trying to Answer
entry.summary: An AI Business column observes that as AI IPOs accelerate, enterprises still struggle to convert experimentation into measurable business outcomes. It frames ROI realization as the core unanswered adoption question.

entry.title: Meta Employees Absolutely Hate Mark Zuckerberg’s Plan for a Companywide AI Hackathon
entry.summary: Wired reports Meta employees strongly oppose Mark Zuckerberg's plan for a companywide AI hackathon, with staff questioning whether the company still supports a hackathon culture. The pushback reflects broader morale problems amid Meta's AI reorganization.

entry.title: Apple’s Camera Chief Thinks AI Can Give You Superpowers
entry.summary: Apple's camera chief Jon McCormack defends generative features in iOS 27's Photos app, which can add synthetic pixels to shots, arguing Apple is not adding AI for its own sake. The framing positions Apple's restrained approach against more aggressive generative imaging.

entry.title: The AI industry's platform trap is starting to look a lot like Microsoft's

entry.title: New OpenAI Academy courses for the next era of work
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced three new Academy courses to help people build practical AI skills, design repeatable workflows, and apply agents in everyday work. The effort targets workforce upskilling for AI adoption.

entry.title: A Coding Implementation on MONAI for End-to-End 3D Spleen Segmentation Using UNet on Medical CT Volumes
entry.summary: MarkTechPost published a hands-on tutorial building a 3D medical CT spleen-segmentation pipeline with MONAI and a 3D UNet, covering preprocessing, mixed-precision training, and sliding-window inference. It is an educational walkthrough rather than new research.
